description: We are a group of enthusiastic students who love learning, science, technology, and exploring Mars. We are quick learners, creative thinkers, and enjoy teamwork and solving problems. We welcome curious and motivated teammates who want to share ideas and take on challenges. Skills in science, engineering, programming, research, or design are a plus. Most importantly, we value creativity, cooperation, and a passion for learning!
summary: Through Viking 1, I was able to see many admirable qualities, such as hard work, diligence, and perseverance. Throughout its journey, it had to overcome extremely harsh conditions, including temperatures ranging from -123°F (-86°C) before sunrise to -27°F (-33°C), as well as rough terrain. Viking 1 also laid the foundation for NASA's future exploration of Mars because it collected and sent valuable data back to NASA. This helped us gain useful information and a better understanding of Mars, including whether life could exist there. Through this project, our group created a poster and a small game to help people learn more about Viking 1 and appreciate its contributions. The poster presents detailed information about Viking 1 and explains why I chose it instead of other spacecraft. Through the poster, I wanted to convey the message that hard work, diligence, and perseverance are important qualities that Viking 1 represents. As for the game, we mainly focused on the process of carrying out its mission. We wanted users to experience what it was like to take on the role of Viking 1 and understand its journey better. To complete this project, we used Canva to design the poster and Google AI Studio to create the game.
details:
People would use our game as a entertainment and education benefit. Our game would start off with a cool entry, showing the Viking 1. We then would get shown about Viking's mission, for the 50 years in just 5 minutes. The intended impact of our project is to let everyone know about robots and spacecraft floating, abandoned in outer space, or even in Mars for 5 whole decades. We used Google AI studio to build our game. Our project is creative because we show what Viking 1 role and duty was. Our team considered education, space and science as a factor for the team.

They will look at our group's poster, which will help users learn more about Viking 1. It is designed to directly engage children aged 8–12 and help them understand Viking 1 better. Our group used Canva to create the poster. We showed our creativity by clearly describing Viking 1's mission and role. We also considered several important factors, such as scientific accuracy, correctness, and visual appeal.
